title: Geofence Telemetry Assembler for Dedicated Tenancy
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: Produce a reproducible, signed bundle of telemetry and control-plane artifacts that demonstrates tenant placement and isolation for Dedicated nodes. The assembler will consume runtime telemetry (node affinity, geolocation tags, lease events), storage retention metadata, and audit logs, then produce a compact, timebound artifact suitable for customer audit, internal compliance reviews, and external attestation (e.g., SOC/ISO evidence ingestion). This ticket implements the collector and assembly pipeline for the initial MVP and defines the canonical bundle format and signing process.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests geofence-tagged events from serving nodes and control plane for a configurable time window
Generated bundle includes: node identifiers, region labels, lease timestamps, retention policy applied, and related audit-log slices
Bundles are signed with the tenant-specific key via KMS and verifiable using provided verification endpoint
End-to-end test demonstrates generation for a simulated dedicated tenant and a verification run that validates included entries
Documentation (console help + runbook) added describing how to request and interpret a bundle
design_notes: We decided on a compact NDJSON bundle wrapped with a manifest.json rather than a monolithic PDF. Manifest lists included slices, their hash, and signature metadata. Trade-off: NDJSON maximizes machine-parseability for automated ingestion by auditor tooling but requires strict schema versioning. For signing, we'll leverage tenant-scoped KMS keys and produce an accompanying detached signature. We evaluated Sigstore but prioritized KMS first due to enterprise key control requirements; Sigstore is listed as a follow-up for public verifiability.
implementation_plan: Add a 'geofence-telemetry' consumer to the runtime event bus that filters lease/grant/revoke and placement-change events
Create an assembler microservice that fetches relevant control-plane snapshots (tenant bindings, reserved pools) and correlates them with telemetry within time window
Canonicalize entries to NDJSON lines and compute per-file SHA256 hashes; generate manifest.json referencing those hashes
Integrate with KMS to sign manifest; persist bundle in tenant-scoped retention bucket with access controls
Expose an internal verification endpoint that verifies signature and returns manifest summary
Add a console action to request bundle generation and a retention policy control in Dedicated tenants UI

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High cardinality of runtime events could blow up bundle size; Mitigation: sample and windowing with configurable heuristics and prioritization of lease/grant events
Risk: Signature key management complexity for shared-responsibility tenants; Mitigation: support both Redwood-managed KMS and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow documented separately
Risk: Latency of assembling large time windows impacts on-demand requests; Mitigation: support scheduled daily export and on-demand snapshot with explicit SLAs
test_plan: Unit tests for NDJSON canonicalizer and hash manifest
Integration test that spins up a simulated dedicated pool, issues placement moves, and verifies the assembler bundle includes expected event slices
Fuzz test for malformed events to ensure assembler rejects and logs anomalies
End-to-end verification with KMS-stub and signature validation
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable assembler for internal dedicated tenants-only; generate daily bundles for 7 days and validate with compliance team
Stage 2: opt-in beta for 3 pilot customers; collect feedback and adjust manifest fields
Stage 3: GA behind RBAC, console toggle, and documented SLAs
